JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 3, Section OBJETIVO E MÉTODO
evidence_quotes.quote: Ao todo, no período 1999/2002 foram pesquisadas 22 comunidades e entrevistadas 188 famílias rurais.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 3, Section OBJETIVO E MÉTODO
evidence_quotes.quote: Como o objetivo do estudo não era quantificar escassez ou abundância do recurso, não houve preocupação com análise estatística. Buscava-se compreender percepções e atitudes, informações fundamentalmente qualitativas.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 5, Section POPULAÇÃO E RECURSOS
evidence_quotes.quote: Primeira: apesar de instituir uma gestão participativa —por meio dos comitês de bacia hidrográfica formado por representantes dos usuários, sociedade civil e poderes públicos— a Lei esvazia o poder dos comitês ao centralizar, na Agência Nacional das Águas (ANA), a decisão final sobre projetos nas bacias hidrográficas

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 6, Section POPULAÇÃO E RECURSOS
evidence_quotes.quote: Quarta: a Lei ignora e afronta a gestão comunitária local ao definir água como bem econômico, cuja disponibilidade deve ser autorizada por meio de outorga e pagamento.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 8, Section PERCEPÇÕES DE ÁGUA
evidence_quotes.quote: Noutros casos, manifesta-se a escassez quando as nascentes perderam muito em volume, obrigando famílias a fazer rodízio para coletar água dos minadouros; em algumas situações só a coletam a cada 3 dias e apenas para parte do consumo doméstico; nesses casos, não há possibilidade de banho e lavagem de roupas todos os dias.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 15, Section CONSUMIDORES, ACORDOS E DESACORDOS
evidence_quotes.quote: Mas, em geral, para fomentar o conservacionismo nas comunidades, as agências e órgãos públicos têm preferido repressão policial, multas e propaganda conservacionista focada em rios e lagos: todos, valores urbanos.

country.comment: Fieldwork conducted in six municipalities of the Jequitinhonha Valley in northeastern Minas Gerais, Brazil, alongside institutional analysis of Brazil's national Water Law (Law No. 9,433/1997).
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title & Section INTRODUÇÃO; PDF pp. 2-3, Section OBJETIVO E MÉTODO; PDF p. 5, Section POPULAÇÃO E RECURSOS

effect_estimate.comment: Purely qualitative study with no statistical estimation of treatment effects; secondary DNAEE (2001) composition figures for the Paraíba do Sul basin committee (40% corporate users, 35% public sector, 25% civil society) are cited descriptively to illustrate unequal representation.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Customary rural norms in the Jequitinhonha Valley govern springs as a non-mercantile collective resource ('dom') that cannot be denied to neighbors and is shared through local rationing during scarcity (e.g., 3-day collection rotations), whereas Brazil's Water Law (Law No. 9,433/1997) and regulatory agencies define water as an economic good subject to permits ('outorga') and charges, centralize final decisions in the National Water Agency (ANA), privilege corporate users in river basin committees (e.g., 40% corporate users, 35% government, and 25% civil society in the Paraíba do Sul committee) while excluding smallholders, and rely on police repression and fines rather than dialogue, leaving rural families facing spring depletion or dam/irrigation appropriation to rely on municipal water trucks and political patronage in villages.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 3, Section OBJETIVO E MÉTODO; PDF pp. 5-6, Section POPULAÇÃO E RECURSOS; PDF pp. 8-10, Section PERCEPÇÕES DE ÁGUA; PDF pp. 11-13, Section ESCASSEZ, COSTUME E MOBILIDADE ESPACIAL; PDF pp. 14-15, Section CONSUMIDORES, ACORDOS E DESACORDOS

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 by the qualitative study design ceiling (CASP Qualitative Checklist). Assigned 2 because fieldwork across 22 rural communities directly documents how customary spring tenure and sharing norms, rationing practices, municipal political patronage in village water provision, exclusion from statutory basin governance, and conservation policing/fines operate on rural water access.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 2-3, Section OBJETIVO E MÉTODO; PDF pp. 5-6, Section POPULAÇÃO E RECURSOS; PDF pp. 8-15

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines customary collective vs. private land/spring tenure and statutory water-use permits/'outorga' (ELIGIBILITY: tenure, property), statutory water user charges/'pagamento' (BURDEN: fees), discretionary political patronage/'apadrinhamento' in municipal water provision, unequal representation in river basin committees, centralization in ANA, and disconnection between basin regulators and municipal governments (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION: discretion, participation, institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination), as well as environmental police repression and fines alongside customary community sanctions (ENFORCEMENT: sanction).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, ENFORCEMENT, tenure, property, fees, discretion, sanction, participation, institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 5-6, Section POPULAÇÃO E RECURSOS; PDF pp. 8-9, Section PERCEPÇÕES DE ÁGUA; PDF pp. 12-15, Sections ESCASSEZ, COSTUME E MOBILIDADE ESPACIAL & CONSUMIDORES, ACORDOS E DESACORDOS

outcome_flags.comment: Examines rural households' access to springs, streams, cisterns, and municipal water trucks (water_access), volumetric depletion and rationing such as 3-day spring collection rotations (service_quantity), and cultural/physical water quality hierarchies distinguishing pure spring water from polluted impounded or river water (service_quality).
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF p. 2, Section OBJETIVO E MÉTODO; PDF pp. 8-11, Section PERCEPÇÕES DE ÁGUA; PDF pp. 11-13, Section ESCASSEZ, COSTUME E MOBILIDADE ESPACIAL

publication_year.comment: Accepted on 05/01/2003 ('Recebido em 02/10/2002 e aceito em 05/01/2003') and published in the combined double issue Ambiente & Sociedade Vol. V, no. 2 (Aug./Dec. 2002) - Vol. VI, no. 1 (Jan./Jul. 2003).
publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, bottom acceptance note; PDF p. 2, journal running header

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Primary qualitative empirical study conducting semi-structured interviews with 188 rural families and community discussion meetings across 22 rural communities, with explicitly qualitative analysis and no statistical component.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF pp. 2-3, Section OBJETIVO E MÉTODO

sample_size.comment: Between 1999 and 2002, researcher pairs interviewed 3 to 4 families per community (188 rural families total) and held post-interview community discussion meetings across 22 rural communities in 6 municipalities (Turmalina, Veredinha, Medina, Joaíma, Monte Formoso, and Jequitinhonha).
sample_size.value: 22 rural communities and 188 rural families interviewed across 6 municipalities
sample_size.where_found: PDF pp. 2-3, Section OBJETIVO E MÉTODO

study_design.comment: Qualitative field investigation conducted in 1999-2002 combining private semi-structured family interviews, collective community discussion meetings, and institutional/legal analysis comparing customary rural water norms with Brazil's Federal Water Law (Law No. 9,433/1997); explicitly reports no statistical analysis.
study_design.value: Qualitative field study (semi-structured family interviews, community discussion meetings, and institutional analysis of water legislation)
study_design.where_found: PDF pp. 2-4, Section OBJETIVO E MÉTODO
